summary: The statement and proof are correct. The ordered same-parity bijection and quadratic identity establish all Gaussian identities without a diagonal assumption or a condition on the shifted minimum. The parity-marginal estimate, likelihood-ratio band bounds, and short-vector case cover all possibilities. In the short-vector case, the shifted Gaussian sum lower bound and closed-interval lattice count rigorously give band probability at most one half, including degenerate intervals and arbitrary shifts; the constants 145, 290, and 435 follow as stated. The finite extension is globally log-concave even for lower-dimensional convex sets. The two conditioning orders give the exact truncation identities, and total variation, the parity-excess comparison, and the endpoint density bound give the finite inequality and tail comparison. Boundary cases, singleton truncations, and one-dimensional concentration limits introduce no errors or gaps.
